summary: Built a small Node.js + Mongoose sample app that demonstrates an immutable transaction ledger on Azure DocumentDB. It atomically writes a Transaction document and updates an Account balance snapshot inside a multi-document transaction, and enforces idempotency via a unique transactionRef index. The app includes a REST API surface, idempotent seed script, a demo script that exercises posting a transaction and a duplicate attempt, and index-creation on startup. Verification was performed against the provided cluster (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and indexes/collections were inspected via the documentdb MCP server.
how_to_run:
1) Install dependencies: npm install
2) Configure environment: copy .env.example to .env and set DOCUMENTDB_URI (the sample uses MONGODB_DATABASE=sample_banking_03 by default).
3) Seed sample accounts (idempotent): npm run seed
4) Start the API server: npm start  (server creates indexes before accepting writes)
5) Demo (alternative to starting server): npm run demo (connects directly and posts a transaction, then attempts a duplicate to show idempotency)
6) Check indexes (prints indexes via driver): npm run check-indexes

Notes:
- Do NOT commit your connection string. Keep DOCUMENTDB_URI in environment variables. The sample reads process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI and process.env.MONGODB_DATABASE (default sample_banking_03).
verification_done: node src/seed.js: ran successfully (output: 'Seed complete'; existing accounts were detected and skipped on this run)

node src/demo.js: ran successfully — created a transaction (+100) and then attempted a duplicate with the same transactionRef which was rejected; account balance reflected only the first post (demonstrates atomicity + idempotency).
documentdb_list_databases (connection_profile: default, db_name: sample_banking_03): returned collections and document counts (accounts: 3, transactions: 4).

documentdb_list_indexes (connection_profile: default, db_name: sample_banking_03, collection: transactions): returned indexes including unique index on transactionRef and compound index on { accountId:1, createdAt:-1 }.
not_verified: Starting and testing the HTTP API via automated HTTP integration tests (I exercised transactional logic via the demo script which calls the same internal function; I did not run npm start and perform HTTP requests during verification).
Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC/RBAC) authentication path was not implemented or tested; sample defaults to SCRAM via DOCUMENTDB_URI as recommended in the readiness guidance.
No unit tests or CI integration were run; the project includes no test-suite (only demo/seed scripts).
No Azure resource provisioning was performed (policy forbids creating resources).
open_issues: Mongoose version selection: I used dependency range "^7.0.0" to allow npm to pick a valid 7.x release in the environment. If you prefer an exact pinned patch version for reproducibility, update package.json accordingly.

mongosh is not installed in this environment; manual interactive checks were performed via the documentdb MCP server and programmatic scripts. If you want a local shell, install mongosh as recommended in the readiness report.
The app's Account.balance is a Number; for production you might prefer Decimal128 or a dedicated money library to avoid floating-point rounding issues.
